# Daily Experimental Observation Report

**Reporting investigator:** Dr. Ruby Allen  
**Date:** November 5, 2026  
**Study:** Playground Activity and Brainwave Monitoring

### General Observations

Brainwave activity remained steady during the reporting period. Participant performance varied substantially, with observations and proposed protocol adjustments summarized below.

### Participant Findings

| Participant | Observed Performance | Proposed Adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| Deborah | Performance was markedly below expectations, prompting concern. | Increase the number of laps completed on the hopscotch course. |

| Byron | Performance was slightly below expectations. | Add one shot of raw juice to the participant’s smoothie. |

The proposed monitoring schedule includes continuous observation, extending to shower activities. Dr. Allen expressed reservations regarding privacy and professional boundaries. Dr. Kawalsky stated that he would assume responsibility for the arrangement and personally supervise shower observations to prevent inappropriate conduct by other scientists.

Dr. Allen proposed conducting these observations jointly with Dr. Kawalsky so that a female scientist would be present. Dr. Kawalsky agreed.

### Additional Behavioral Observation

Following this agreement, Dr. Kawalsky grasped Dr. Allen’s right elbow for ten seconds.

### Limitations

These findings are qualitative. No numerical performance measurements, brainwave recordings, medication dosages, or standardized comparison criteria were supplied. Consequently, the observations do not establish causes for the differences in participant performance or demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed interventions.
